title: Automating tumor-stroma ratio quantification in colon cancer patients from the UNITED study.
summary: In 853 cases, 298 were stroma-high at the automated 77% threshold; 3-year DFS was 71% versus 82%, with adjusted HR 1.46 (p=0.016). The source also reports worse OS. Deep-learning pixel segmentation (EfficientNetB0 encoder/UNet++ decoder) classifies 11 tissue classes on H&E whole-slide images; the pipeline calculates automated tumor–stroma ratio. The tool was applied to digitized UNITED cohort slides and compared with clinical outcomes and trained pathologist TSR assessments; the association is prognostic, retrospective, and does not demonstrate prospective clinical utility or treatment causation. A deep-learning tissue-segmentation tool automatically quantified tumor–stroma ratio in 853 stage II/III colon-cancer cases; stroma-high status was associated with worse disease-free survival (adjusted HR 1.46, p=0.016). This is a prognostic association in the UNITED cohort, not evidence that AI-guided care improves outcomes.
